title: Fix battery status reading a phantom BAT device on dual-bay ThinkPads
head: bd6e75c6c04a
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates
outcome: completed: one confirmed gap (decimal-comma locale defeats selection), two optional test improvements, description and related-PR notes

leads.summary: A comma-decimal UPower energy-full prevents selection of the populated BAT1
leads.consequence: Under a locale that prints `energy-full: 56,4 Wh`, the regex rejects the populated pack; with phantom BAT0 enumerated first, the power notification and --shell status continue reporting BAT0 (0% and 0Wh). The existing percentage/capacity parser also assumes dot decimals, but the newly introduced selection makes this input unable to recover from the phantom.

leads.summary: Missing native-path silently drops previously available cycles and thresholds
leads.consequence: If `upower -i` returns battery status but omits/empties native-path, the old BAT* fallback still showed cycle count and sysfs charge limits; the new script suppresses both although BAT0 sysfs files are readable. In the power panel this changes Charge cycles to an em dash and a charge-limit label to a dash. This input is exceptional for the normal Linux UPower power_supply backend, whose native path is the device name.
leads.triage: already_in_opus_final (Q2/F3, absolute or missing native-path); unreachable with current UPower; published within the native-path optional test note

leads.summary: Added dual-bay test bypasses the changed sysfs threshold fallback
leads.consequence: BAT1 supplies both charge thresholds directly in the stubbed `upower -i` response, so the asserted 75-80% never tests the new `battery_path/charge_control_*_threshold` reads. A regression that still reads BAT0 thresholds, or drops the sysfs fallback, can pass this specific threshold assertion. Extend the fixture with different BAT0/BAT1 sysfs thresholds and omit them from UPower output.

leads.summary: Open PR #12484 expects a sibling cycle count that this PR intentionally suppresses
leads.consequence: If both PRs are merged while retaining this PR's selected-pack-only cycles code, #12484's existing BAT0=0/BAT1=450 test fails: this PR emits cycles 0, not the sibling's 450. The scripts also edit the same cycles assignment, so a manual decision on whether cycle counts describe the selected pack or any available pack is needed. This is a cross-PR compatibility lead, not a defect on this PR alone.
leads.triage: factual; coordinator confirmed from sol/pr-12484-files.json patch (test expects cycles 450 from BAT1 when BAT0=0); Opus draft-check also confirmed

limits: No real UPower, D-Bus, sysfs or desktop was queried. Isolated runs exercise stub-defined inputs only; source evidence from upstream UPower commit ce25d69fe1b1e871964f39d8a0d0c7a0e8059809, not a proven Omarchy-distribution pinned UPower package version.
The normal Linux UPower power_supply native-path is nonempty and relative according to upstream; H2 is a missing-field resilience regression, not evidence that ordinary batteries omit native-path.
Related open PRs were fetched as GitHub patch metadata; cross-PR merges were reasoned from patches and isolated #12484-shaped input, not an actual merged tree or full PR test run.
The existing base/head battery-status-test.sh was not run wholesale. Source inspection establishes its single BAT0 fixture remains valid; the isolated comparisons cover named boundary cases.

flags.claim: Six open PRs rewrite the same `upower -e | grep BAT | head -n 1` line with other strategies (#7373, #10392, #12024, #12445, #12789, #13029).
Or a separator-neutral check: `awk -v v="$candidate_energy_full" 'BEGIN { sub(/,/, ".", v); exit !(v + 0 > 0) }'`. It changed no other tested case.
On a dual-bay machine in a decimal-comma locale, the power panel details and the battery notification (omarchy-notification-battery) keep showing the phantom's 0% as before.
One gap remains: the new selection check only accepts a dot as the decimal separator, so the fix does not apply under decimal-comma locales such as `de_DE`.
Reverting the threshold fallback ... still passes all three tests, because the BAT1 stub prints its thresholds in the `upower -i` text (test lines 93-94), so the sysfs fallback is never read.

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** With the unpopulated bay listed first and reporting `energy-full: 0 Wh`, the script now reports the installed battery, and cycle count and sysfs thresholds come from that same device. One gap remains: the new selection check only accepts a dot as the decimal separator, so under decimal-comma locales such as `de_DE` the fix does not apply when the real pack's capacity has a fractional part.

```text
phantom BAT0 (energy-full 0 Wh) listed before real BAT1, C locale, stub upower
base  percentage 0%    state unknown    cycles 0
head  percentage 68%   state charging   cycles 80   threshold 75-80%
```

**Verified:** Base and head give byte-identical `--shell` and text output for two real packs, a single pack (named BAT0 or BAT1, with thresholds only in sysfs, or reporting `energy-full` 0), a real BAT0 with an empty second bay, no battery, and a failing `upower -e`. An empty bay reported as `present: no` is also skipped, because UPower reports `energy-full` 0 for a pack that is not present. The new phantom test fails on the base script and passes on the head, and the existing test still passes against the head script.

### The phantom is still selected under decimal-comma locales

The candidate check (`bin/omarchy-battery-status:38`) accepts `energy-full` only if it matches `^[0-9]+([.][0-9]+)?$`. The `upower` CLI calls `setlocale(LC_ALL, "")` (`tools/up-tool.c`) and prints `energy-full` with `%g` (`libupower-glib/up-device.c`), which follows `LC_NUMERIC`. GLib's `%g` printed `56.4 Wh` under C.UTF-8 and `56,4 Wh` under `de_DE`. With a stub `upower` serving that comma output:

```text
phantom BAT0 (0 Wh) listed before real BAT1 (56,4 Wh), stub upower
base  percentage 0%   state unknown   cycles 0
head  percentage 0%   state unknown   cycles 0    56,4 fails the check, first candidate kept
```

The real `upower` binary was not run. The comma output is based on UPower source plus the GLib result above. A pack whose `energy-full` prints as a whole number has no separator and would still qualify (from the regex, not run).

**Impact:** On a dual-bay machine in a decimal-comma locale, with the unpopulated bay listed first, the power panel details and the battery notification (`omarchy-notification-battery`) keep showing the phantom's 0% as before. The power panel starts `omarchy-battery-status --shell` without a locale override.

**Suggested change:** In an isolated run, either change made the scenario above report `68%`, `charging`, `cycles 80` and `threshold 75-80%`:
- `candidate_info=$(LC_ALL=C upower -i "$candidate")`, the pattern `bin/omarchy-network-band` already uses for localized tool output. Its only other effect in the tested cases: a single pack in a comma locale reports `time 2h 30m` instead of `2h`, because the existing `time to empty` parser also truncates `2,5 hours`.
- Or replace both the regex and the `> 0` test on line 38 with one separator-neutral check: `if awk -v v="$candidate_energy_full" 'BEGIN { sub(/,/, ".", v); exit !(v + 0 > 0) }'; then`. It changed no other tested case.

### Notes

**Optional test improvement:** Two changed paths are not covered. Reverting the threshold fallback (`bin/omarchy-battery-status:89-90`) to the old `BAT*/charge_control_*_threshold | head -1` glob still passes all three tests: no fixture writes `charge_control_*_threshold` files, and the BAT1 stub prints its thresholds in the `upower -i` text (test lines 93-94). Removing the first-candidate default (line 36) also passes, although a single pack reporting `energy-full` 0 then prints an empty percentage and state. Dropping the threshold lines from BAT1's stub text, writing different `charge_control_*_threshold` files into both bays, and adding a single-pack `energy-full: 0 Wh` case would cover both.

**Optional test improvement:** The unresolvable `native-path` test passes with the new guard (lines 65-67) replaced by the base assignment, so it does not check the behavior its comment describes. Current UPower reports `native-path` for power_supply devices as a bare name such as `BAT1` (`src/linux/up-native.c`). With an absolute or missing `native-path`, the head drops cycles and sysfs thresholds that the base still found through its `BAT*` glob; current UPower does not produce that input.

**Description:** The bar percentage, bar icon and low-battery warning read `UPower.displayDevice`, not this script. The fix is visible in the power panel details and the battery notification.

**Related PRs:** Seven open PRs rewrite the same `upower -e | grep BAT | head -n 1` line with other strategies (#7373, #7965, #10392, #12024, #12445, #12789, #13029). #12484 also changes the `cycle_count` line and its tests expect a sibling pack's count when BAT0 reports 0; this PR reports only the selected pack's value. Whichever lands later needs a manual merge.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Pinned head `bd6e75c` against merge base `7b336b1`. Base and head scripts run in isolation with a stub `upower` and synthetic power_supply trees across 14 scenarios in both output modes, plus the PR's test file on head and base and diagnostic mutants of the changed lines. GLib number formatting was checked under C.UTF-8 and a privately compiled `de_DE` locale. The real `upower` daemon, D-Bus and hardware sysfs were not used, and no ThinkPad hardware was tested.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
